Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:10:1.hebrew: ולא ימיר אותו טוב ברע - דהיינו בעל מום. אם המר ימיר — יהיה קדש, אפילו בעל מום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:10:1.english: Nor substitute it, a good for a bad - That is, a blemished [animal. And the verse continues:] “If he shall at all substitute [animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is substituted] shall be holy” — even a blemished [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:12:1.english: Offspring - Blemished [animals] that were born from unblemished consecrated [animals].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:1.hebrew: פסקה תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל - מקרא אחרינא, ולא איצטריך האי להכי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:1.english: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael ruled it - [From] another verse, and this [verse] was not needed for this [purpose].

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:2.hebrew: רק קדשיך וגו' אלו התמורות - דאתא לאשמועינן שיקרבו למזבח. דאי לעיקר הקדש אתא, למה לי למכתב שיעלם לירושלים? הא שמעינן קראי טובא: ״השמר לך פן תעלה עולותיך וגו'״:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:2.english: “Only your sacred items” etc., these are the substitutes - For it comes to teach us that they are to be offered on the altar. For if it came [to refer] to primary consecrated [animals], why did [the verse] need to write that he should bring them up to Jerusalem? Behold, we have heard many verses [teaching this]: “Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings etc.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:4.hebrew: אף הני בעל מום לא - הלכך, כי אתא לא תזבח — לבמת יחיד אתא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:13:4.english: These too [are] not [sacrificed if] blemished - Therefore, when [the verse] “You shall not sacrifice” came, it came [to apply] to a private altar.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:14:1.hebrew: השתא רע בטוב אמרת לא - שלא יביא בהמת חולין תמימים אצל בהמת קודש בעל מום, ויאמר: זו תמורת זו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:14:1.english: Now that you have said that “a bad for a good” [is] not [permitted] - That he may not bring an unblemished non-sacred animal alongside a blemished consecrated animal and say: “This is in exchange for that.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:14:2.english: Rather - It is for this [reason] that “a good for a bad” is written.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:14:3.hebrew: טוב מעיקרו - שנתפס בקדושה כשהוא תמים, עושה תמורה אע"פ שהומם, כדכתיב: "או רע בטוב", דמשמע: רע של קודש בטוב של חולין, דרע של קודש עושה תמורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:14:3.english: Good at the outset - [An animal] that was seized with sanctity when it was unblemished effects substitution even though it became blemished, as it is written: "or a bad for a good," which implies a bad [animal] of consecrated [status] [exchanged] for a good [animal] of non-sacred [status], for a bad [animal] of consecrated [status] effects substitution.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:15:1.hebrew: זו דברי רבי שמעון - דאמר בפרק בתרא דתמורה (דף לב.), קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:15:1.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon - As he said in the last chapter of Temurah (daf 32a): Items consecrated to the altar were included in [the requirement of] standing and valuation.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:16:1.hebrew: דתנן ר' שמעון אומר כו' - ומדאמר רבי שמעון קדשי בדק הבית לא היו, מכלל דקרא בקדשי מזבח כתיב, והכא מודה בבעל מום מעיקרא דנפדה, אע"ג דקדשי מזבח. וממאי דתנא דמתני' סבירא ליה קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה, שצריכין שיהו חיין בשעת פדייה, כדכתיב: "והעמיד את הבהמה לפני הכהן", ואח"כ: "והעריך אותה"? מדקתני סיפא גבי קדם הקדשן את מומן, דאגב שקידשן למזבח מקדישין תמימים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:16:1.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says, etc. - And from [the fact] that Rabbi Shimon said [that] items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included in standing and valuation], by implication the verse is written regarding items consecrated for the altar; and here, he concedes regarding [an animal that was] blemished from the outset that it is redeemed, even though [it is of] items consecrated for the altar. And from where [is it known] that the tanna of our Mishnah holds [that] items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation, which require that they be alive at the time of redemption, as it is written: “Then he shall stand the animal before the priest,” and afterward: “and [the priest] shall appraise it”? From [the fact] that the latter clause teaches regarding [animals whose] consecration preceded their blemish [that if they died they must be buried] — as since he consecrated them for the altar, they consecrate unblemished [animals]:

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:17:1.hebrew: אבל חכמים - לאו הנך רבנן דפליגי עליה דר' שמעון במס' תמורה — דהתם אמרינן: לדברי הכל בעל מום מעיקרו לא היה בכלל העמדה והערכה — אלא תנא דבי לוי הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:17:1.english: But the Rabbis - [These are] not those Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon in Tractate Temurah — for there we say: According to all, [an animal that was] blemished from the outset was not included in [the requirement of] standing and valuation — but rather, it is the tanna of the school of Levi.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:18:1.hebrew: אפי' חיה - דאינה ראויה למזבח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:18:1.english: Even an undomesticated animal - For it is not fit for the altar.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:19:1.english: Indeed so, that if they died they may be redeemed - For regarding [an animal with] a blemish from the outset, they agree.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:1:1.hebrew: נפדין תמימים - אותן וולדות שנולדו לפני פדיונן, או אין נפדין תמימים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:1:1.english: Are they redeemed unblemished - [Are] those offspring that were born before their [mothers'] redemption [redeemed unblemished], or are they not redeemed unblemished?

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:2:2.english: Primary - The mother. Evidently, [the offspring] may be redeemed [while] unblemished.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:3:1.hebrew: וקא דייק הש"ס טעמא - דלא בעי מום משום דלא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר, דמכח בעל מום אתו. הא לא אתו מכח בעל מום, אלא לדידהו מקדיש להו לדמיהן — לא נפקי לחולין בלא מום, דקדוש קדושת הגוף:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:3:1.english: And the Gemara infers: “The reason” - That [the offspring] do not require a blemish [is only] because the subsidiary should not be more stringent than the primary, since they come by virtue of a blemished [animal]. But had they not come by virtue of a blemished [animal], but rather one consecrated them themselves for their value, they would not go out to non-sacred status without a blemish, for they are sanctified with inherent sanctity.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:3:3.hebrew: הקדיש זכר לדמיו - שימכרנו ויביא בדמיו עולה — הוא עצמו קדוש קדושת הגוף, ויקרב עולה. להכי נקט זכר דחזי לעולה, משום דרובא דמייתו קרבן — עולה מייתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:3:3.english: [If] one consecrated a male for its value - [Intending] that he sell it and bring a burnt-offering with its proceeds — it itself is sanctified with inherent sanctity and shall be sacrificed [as] a burnt-offering. For this reason [the Tanna] specified a male, which is fit for a burnt-offering, because most [people] who bring a [voluntary] offering bring a burnt-offering.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:4:1.hebrew: רבי אלעזר מתני - השוחט בחוץ חייב. לאו כרת קאמר, אלא מלקות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:4:1.english: Rabbi Elazar teaches - [That] one who slaughters outside is liable. He did not mean karet [excision], but rather lashes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:4:2.hebrew: ומוקי - להאי חוץ, כגון ששחטו בבמת יחיד בשעת היתר הבמות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:4:2.english: And he interprets - this [term] “outside” [as referring to a case] such as where he slaughtered it on a private altar at a time when private altars were permitted:

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:5:1.hebrew: במת יחיד - שכל אחד ואחד בונה במה לעצמו, כגון במת מנוח וגדעון ושמואל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:5:1.english: An altar of an individual - Where each and every person builds an altar for himself, such as the altar of Manoah, Gideon, and Samuel.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:5:2.hebrew: במה גדולה - נוב וגבעון, שהן של צבור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:5:2.english: A great altar - Nob and Gibeon, which belong to the community:

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:6:1.english: Since it is sanctified [while] blemished - To be forbidden for shearing and labor.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:8:1.english: And say: If it is not [referring to] the matter, etc. - And [the verse is] still [referring] to a great altar.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:8:2.hebrew: לא יבקר - לא יבדוק בין תם לבעל מום, דאיזה שיהא עשירי יהא קדוש:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:8:2.english: He shall not inquire - He shall not inspect between an unblemished [animal] and a blemished one, for whichever is the tenth shall be sacred.

Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:9:1.hebrew: גמר העברה העברה מבכור - מה בכור בעל מום לא קרב, אף מעשר בעל מום לא. כי אתא קרא — לבמת יחיד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 14b:9:1.english: It is derived [from the verbal analogy of] "passing" [and] "passing" from a firstborn - Just as a blemished firstborn is not sacrificed, so too a blemished [animal] tithe is not [sacrificed]. When the verse came, [it was to apply] to a private altar.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:13:1.hebrew: הקישן הכתוב לנדרים - אינו מן (כן) הברייתא בתמורה פרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יז:), ורבא מפרש כן בפני עצמו. ולקמן (בכורות דף טו:) בשמעתין יש ברייתא אחרת דמפקא תמורת וולדות מזכר ונקבה, ופליגא אתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל דהכא, כדמפרש בתמורה (דף יז:); וכן פי' לקמן בקונטרס. וההוא תנא נמי נפקא שפיר, שהקישה תמורות וולדות לגוף הקרבן — דבגוף הקרבן איירי "אם זכר ואם נקבה", אלא דמיתורא דרשינן נמי תמורות וולדות; ומהשתא, לא צריכא להקישא דלעיל דמקיש תמורתו לו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:13:1.english: "The verse juxtaposed them to vows" - [This clause] is not from [variant: so in] the baraita in Temurah, in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Kodashim (Temurah 17b); rather, Rava explains it this way on his own. And later (Bekhorot 15b) in our sugya, there is another baraita that derives substitutes and offspring from "male and female" (Leviticus 3:1), and it disagrees with the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael here, as [the Gemara] explains in Temurah (17b); and so Rashi explains later. And according to that tanna as well, it is derived well, for [the verse] juxtaposed substitutes and offspring to the offering itself — since "whether male or whether female" refers to the offering itself, but from the superfluity we also derive substitutes and offspring. And now [according to that tanna], [the Gemara] does not need the juxtaposition above, which juxtaposes its substitute to it.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:14:1.hebrew: טוב ברע מיבעיא - הך סוגיא דפ"ק דתמורה (דף ט.). ורבא סבר: אין מזהירין (עונשין) מן הדין, ודריש התם בע"א; ואביי לא חשיב ליה דינא, דמי גרעי? ונקט הכא דרשא דאביי, לפי שפשוט לו יותר. וכהאי גוונא איכא בסנהדרין (דף לד:) גבי "אין רואין את הנגעים אלא ביום", ומייתי עלה דרשה דאביי: "דביום" — ולא בלילה, ושביק דרשא דרבא דמפיק ליה מ"לי ולא לאורי". ואין לתמוה: מהא ד"אלו נשרפין" (סנהדרין עו.) איכא איפכא גבי בתו מאנוסתו, דאמר ק"ו: "בת בתו ענש, על בתו לא כל שכן?", וחשיב ליה (לו) אביי גלוי מילתא טפי מרבא, (ולא) גמרינן מהדדי? דגבי אחותו איצטריך קרא לכולי עלמא לבת אביו ובת אמו משום דאין מזהירין מן הדין, ולא חשיבא ליה גלויי מילתא בעלמא — היינו משום דפשטיה דקרא משמע שבא למעט, דכתיב: "בת אביו או בת אמו":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:14:1.english: Is it necessary [to state] "good for bad"? - This sugya is from the first chapter of Temurah (9a). And Rava holds that one does not warn (or punish) based on an a fortiori inference, and he expounds [the verse] there in a different manner; whereas Abaye does not consider it an [independent] derivation, for is [good] worse [than bad]? And [the Gemara] here adopted the derivation of Abaye because it is simpler for it. And similarly, there is [a case] in Sanhedrin (34b) regarding "one does not examine afflictions except during the day," where it cites concerning it the derivation of Abaye, that "during the day" [means] and not at night, and leaves aside the derivation of Rava, who derives it from "to me" — and not to my light. And one should not wonder: from that which is [taught in the chapter entitled] "Elu Hanisrafin" (Sanhedrin 76a), is it the reverse regarding his daughter from a raped woman — where he stated an a fortiori inference: "If He punished [for] his daughter's daughter, is it not all the more so [punishable for] his daughter?", and Abaye considers it a clarification of the matter more than Rava — (and do we not) derive [these cases] from one another? For regarding his sister, according to all opinions a verse was necessary for the daughter of his father and daughter of his mother because "one does not warn based on an a fortiori inference," and [Abaye] did not consider it a mere clarification of the matter — that is because the plain meaning of the verse implies that it comes to exclude, as it is written: "the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:14:2.hebrew: טוב ברע מיבעיא - ואם תאמר: דלמא איצטריך משום סיפא דקרא: "והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קודש"? וי"ל: דהוה מצי למיכתב בסיפיה: "ואם המר ימיר טוב ברע או רע בטוב":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:14:2.english: Is "a good for a bad" necessary? - And if you should say: Perhaps it was necessary because of the latter part of the verse: "then it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy"? And one can say: It could have written in its latter part: "And if he shall at all substitute a good for a bad or a bad for a good."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:16:1.hebrew: ומודה ר"ש בבעל מום מעיקרו - למאי דאמרינן בסמוך, דרב סבר כר"ל [דאמר התם] לרבנן: קדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה — ניחא דמודה לרבנן; אבל למאי דמסקינן דסבר כר' יוחנן, דלרבנן אחד זה ואחד זה היו בכלל העמדה והערכה — אם כן, מודה למאן? ויש לפרש: דנקט הכי דלא תיסק אדעתא טעמא דמתניתין משום דאין פודין לאכילה לכלבים, ולא משום העמדה והערכה, דלא בעינן בקדשי מזבח העמדה והערכה, ולכך ברישא, דקדם מומן, יפדו; והשתא קמ"ל דטעמא דמתני' משום העמדה והערכה — וכדדייקינן בסמוך מדלא קתני: "ואם נעשו טריפה" — וברישא, דקדם מומן, מודה רבי שמעון דלא בעי העמדה והערכה. והשתא דנקט "מודה רבי שמעון", משום דאיכא למיטעי דפליג אמתני' כדפרישית, איצטריך למימר דשפיר מודה בה. והא דנקט רבי שמעון — משום דלדידיה פשיטא ליה טפי דקדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה, מדקאמר: קדשי בדק הבית לא היו, ע"כ כי כתיבא העמדה והערכה בקדשי מזבח כתיבא; אבל לרבנן, לא פשיטא ליה כולי האי, דמצי למימר: "לא היו", כמו שאומר ריש לקיש:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:16:1.english: "And Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to [an animal] blemished from the outset" - According to what we say nearby, that Rav held in accordance with Reish Lakish [who said there] that according to the Rabbis, altar consecrations were not included in standing and valuation, it is well understood that he concedes to the Rabbis. But according to what we conclude, that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, that according to the Rabbis, both this and that were included in standing and valuation — if so, to whom is he conceding? And it can be explained that it formulated [the statement] this way so that it should not enter [one's] mind that the reason of our Mishnah is because one may not redeem [sacrificial animals] to feed them to dogs, and not because of standing and valuation — [thinking] that we do not require standing and valuation for altar consecrations, and therefore in the first clause, where their blemish preceded [their consecration], they may be redeemed; and now it teaches us that the reason of our Mishnah is because of standing and valuation — as we infer nearby from the fact that it did not teach: "and if they became a tereifah [they must be buried]" — and in the first clause, where their blemish preceded [their consecration], Rabbi Shimon concedes that it does not require standing and valuation. And now that it stated "Rabbi Shimon concedes" — because one could have mistakenly thought that he disagrees with our Mishnah, as I explained, it was necessary to state that he indeed concedes to it. And this [fact] that it formulated [this regarding] Rabbi Shimon is because to him it was more obvious that altar consecrations were included in standing and valuation, since he said: "Temple maintenance consecrations were not [included]," perforce when standing and valuation is written, it is written regarding altar consecrations; but according to the Rabbis, it was not that obvious to him, for one could say they were not [included], just as Reish Lakish says.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:16:2.hebrew: אותה למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרו - כל קדשי בדק הבית, לרבי שמעון, ממעטינן מקרא אחרינא בסוף תמורה (דף לג.):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:16:2.english: “It” [serves] to exclude [an animal] blemished from the outset - [For] all [items] consecrated for Temple maintenance, according to Rabbi Shimon, we exclude [them] from another verse at the end of Temurah (33a).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:3:1.hebrew: הקדיש זכר לדמיו קדוש קדושת הגוף - להכי נקט זכר — דקרב הוא עצמו עולה; ואי הוה נקט בהמה סתם, הוי אמינא: דנקבה קדוש קדושת הגוף וקרב שלמים. ושמעינן ליה לר' יהושע במסכת שקלים (דף ו.) — ומייתי לה בתמורה פרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כ.) — במקדיש נכסיו: "זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות, ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים ויביא בדמיהם עולות". ומיהו נראה, לר' אליעזר נמי דאמר התם: "זכרים ימכרו לצרכי עולות, ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים, ודמיהם יפלו לשאר נכסים לבדק הבית" — לפי מה שהיה רבא ר"ל מתחלה התם בההוא פירקין: "המקדיש זכר אין קדוש קדושת הגוף", לא קשה ליה מידי ממתני' דשקלים; דיש לחלק בין מקדיש נכסיו סתם, לפירש בהדיא לדמיו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:3:1.english: [If] one consecrated a male for its value, it is sanctified with inherent sanctity - For this reason it specified a male, because it itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering; whereas had it stated "an animal" without specification, I would have said that a female [also] is sanctified with inherent sanctity and sacrificed as a peace offering. And [yet] we have heard that Rabbi Yehoshua in tractate Shekalim (daf 6a) — and it is cited in Temurah in the chapter [entitled] Elu Kodashim (Temurah daf 20a) — [says] regarding one who consecrates his property: "Males themselves shall be sacrificed as burnt offerings, and females shall be sold for the needs of peace offerings, and he shall bring burnt offerings with their proceeds." However, it appears [that] according to Rabbi Eliezer as well, who said there, "Males shall be sold for the needs of burnt offerings, and females shall be sold for the needs of peace offerings, and their proceeds shall fall [along with] the rest of the property to Temple maintenance" — according to what Rava originally intended to say there in that chapter, [namely that] one who consecrates a male is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, nothing was difficult for him from the mishna in Shekalim, as one can distinguish between one who consecrates his property without specification and [one who] explicitly specified [it was] for its value.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:9:1.hebrew: גמר העברה - מצי למימר: "תחת" "תחת" מקדשים; ולפי שהמעשר ובכור שוין בכמה עניינים, נקטיה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 14b:9:1.english: It is derived [from the word] "passing" - [The Gemara] could have said [that it is derived via the verbal analogy of] "under" [and] "under" from sacrificial offerings; but because [animal] tithe and a firstborn are equivalent in several matters, it cited this [derivation].
